HOMAGE TO MARTYRS OF THE QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT 
THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, today is the Sixtieth 
Anniversary of the 'Quit India Movement'. On behalf of the House, I would 
like to pay homage to the martyrs of the 'Quit India Movement". 
Hon. Members, today, the 9 th August, is a historic and momentous 
day in the annals of our nation. It was on this day sixty years ago that the 
'Quit India Movement' was launched against the British rule in India, under 
the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. The whole nation responded to the clarion 
call of Gandhiji and participated with single-minded commitment and 
dedication, which culminated in our achieving Independence, five years later. 
' We pay our humble and respectful homage to all those martyrs who 
laid down their lives, and to all those who underwent untold sufferings for the 
cause of our Independence. 
I would request the hon. Members to rise in their places and observe 
silence as a mark of respect to the memory of martyrs and freedom fighters. 
[Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute]
